== Biography ==
Janet Glasgow is confidently identified with the child baptised at Livingston on 2 February 1777 to [[Glasgow-1382|Thomas Glasgow]] and [[Davidson-14073|Christian (Christine) Davidson]]. Her existing birth bound remains before that day; the baptism supplies no exact birthday.<ref name="Janet1777" />

She is also strongly identified with the daughter Janet who erected the Livingston family memorial for her mother Christian Davidson and father Thomas Glasgow. Her preferred death is 16 October 1853, aged 76, while the companion 16 October 1873 reading is retained as a conflicting version. These are qualified readings of the family memorial, not a newly read stone.<ref name="LivingstonFamilyMI" />

The inherited Bridgeton, Kincardineshire birthplace and Blackburn surname association remain uncertain. “Janet Glasgow, Blackburn” in the inscription may refer to residence; no husband, marriage or married surname is established by that wording.

== Research Notes ==
=== Janet's identity and parental roles ===
The held Livingston baptism names Janet Glasgow, Thomas Glasgow and Christian Davidson on 2 February 1777; one companion gives Livingston residence. These are two indexes of one event, not separate children.<ref name="Janet1777">Findmypast, ''Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564–1929'', [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_685844147&tab=this R_685844147] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_692403113&tab=this R_692403113], Janet Glasgow, baptism 2 February 1777, Livingston, parents Thomas Glasgow and Christian Davidson; held inspected derivatives, original register uninspected.</ref> The memorial explicitly calls Christian Janet's mother and Thomas her father. The full couple, family memorial and chronology support 97% for each existing parent placement. The father's former 43% possible grade is superseded; the mother's 97% is her first individual rating, not a new maternal attachment or a measured rise from an invented earlier percentage.

Age 76 with death in 1853 is compatible with baptism near birth in 1777, although baptism need not have been in infancy. The conflicting 1873/76 combination implies birth around 1797, after the named mother's 1795 death, so those digits cannot all be correct for the same daughter. A correct later death year with a wrong age remains possible. The combined correlation favours 16 October 1853, with 1873 remaining an alternative.

The inherited Bridgeton, Kincardineshire birthplace remains unverified and is retained as a field-level claim, not asserted by the Livingston baptism. The fuller inscription's “Janet Glasgow, Blackburn” may identify a locality; it does not prove a married surname. No husband, marriage or descendants are inferred. An earlier about-1780 birth estimate and firm unsourced parent statement were superseded by the existing before-2-February-1777 bound and the dated assessments. The present family inference replaces the older blanket hold; it does not silently settle the place or surname questions.

=== Memorial readings and source limits ===
The preferred readings come from a combined interpretation of held derivatives, not a new stone reading or source fetch. One Findmypast version gives Thomas's death as 22 July 1831, aged 85; Christian Davidson, 5 November 1795, aged 43; son Peter, 12 September 1810, aged 19; and daughter Janet, 16 October 1853, aged 76. It also names grandchildren Mary Russell, who died in infancy, Jessie Russell, 11 July 1845, aged 20, another Jessie Russell, 8 February 1851, aged ten months, and James B. Russell, 22 April 1854, aged nineteen months.

The fuller companion says Janet Glasgow, Blackburn, erected the memorial for her mother Christian Davidson, who died 5 November 1795 aged 45; Thomas Glasgow her father, 22 May 1831 aged 85; and Peter her brother, 12 September 1819 aged 48. It gives the above Janet's death as 16 October 1873 aged 76, the infant Jessie's date as 8 February 1831, and James B. Russell's year as 185*. These differing month/year/age readings are retained, not harmonised into independent people or new exact facts. Repeated rows under different family names still refer to the same memorial.<ref name="LivingstonFamilyMI">Findmypast, ''Scotland Monumental Inscriptions'', Livingston family memorial, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=PRS%2FSCOTLAND%2FMI%2FADD%2F5%2F00542646&tab=this PRS/SCOTLAND/MI/ADD/5/00542646] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPRS%2FSCOT%2FMIS%2F511333&tab=this GBPRS/SCOT/MIS/511333]; compare the same inscription indexed under Janet as [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=PRS%2FSCOTLAND%2FMI%2FADD%2F5%2F00422894&tab=this PRS/SCOTLAND/MI/ADD/5/00422894] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPRS%2FSCOT%2FMIS%2F511321&tab=this GBPRS/SCOT/MIS/511321], and under Peter as [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=PRS%2FSCOTLAND%2FMI%2FADD%2F5%2F00516377&tab=this PRS/SCOTLAND/MI/ADD/5/00516377] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPRS%2FSCOT%2FMIS%2F511329&tab=this GBPRS/SCOT/MIS/511329]. Held derivative transcriptions captured/reviewed 24–30 October 2026; one physical memorial, not independent witnesses. [https://billiongraves.com/grave/Thomas-Glasgow/3399144 BillionGraves memorial 3399144, marker LV 106] has a competing 1851 Thomas reading and a previously blurred preview; original inscription not newly read.</ref>

BillionGraves instead indexes Thomas's death as 22 May 1851, aged 85, from which the earlier circa-1766 birth was calculated. That is not an independent birth record. The original stone and parish-register images remain uninspected for this reconciliation. A legible inscription or burial record could resolve the disputed digits, but a blanket requirement for an original does not prevent a qualified preferred interpretation of the existing family evidence. No Russell grandchild is assigned a parent profile through these readings alone.

=== Family assessment and next evidence ===
Father Thomas is preferred to have died in 1831 aged 85, with May/July unresolved and 1851 retained as an alternative. Christian's preferred death is 5 November 1795, with age 43/45 unresolved; her approximate birth is not changed. Janet's 97% father and first 97% mother assessments are existing links and share this combined parish/memorial identity argument. The father's own 93% ancestry assessment is a separate proposition, not a multiplier reducing the directly recorded child's parentage.

No date or family assignment is made for Peter or the Russell grandchildren from the conflicting monument versions alone. The original stone and Janet's marriage/death evidence remain useful for the disputed date, place and surname, but the earlier 43%/unassessed-parent blanket hold is no longer the preferred family interpretation. [https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/people/glasgow-1382.html#research-findings Full family reasoning].
